sections.title: Harbor Billing webhook operations, part 1
sections.text: Harbor Billing signs webhook bodies with HMAC-SHA256 over the raw bytes, not over a re-serialized object. The header carries a timestamp and the key id. Receivers should reject timestamps more than five minutes from their clock and should tolerate one overlap key during rotation.

sections.title: Harbor Billing webhook operations, part 2
sections.text: A failed delivery stays in the tenant queue for two days and then moves to a dead-letter list the customer can replay. Replays use the original event id. Receivers that are not idempotent will apply the event twice, which is the receiver's bug.

sections.title: Harbor Billing webhook operations, part 3
sections.text: Egress addresses are published on the status page before they change. Customers with allow lists are expected to read that page. A firewall drop looks the same as an application failure in the delivery log, except the log shows a connection timeout rather than an HTTP status.

sections.title: Harbor Billing webhook operations, part 4
sections.text: Test events use the same signature scheme and a payload type of ping. They are not billing events. A successful ping does not prove that a later invoice event will match the customer's business rules.

sections.title: Lumen Desk identity provisioning, part 1
sections.text: Lumen Desk accepts SCIM users and groups. A group push replaces membership when the replace operation is explicit. An empty member list is rejected when it would remove more than a small threshold, because identity providers sometimes emit an empty page during an upstream failure.

sections.title: Lumen Desk identity provisioning, part 2
sections.text: Deactivating a user keeps their historical tickets and removes their ability to sign in. Rules that store the user id keep storing it. Offboarding reports list those rules so an administrator can point them at a queue.

sections.title: Lumen Desk identity provisioning, part 3
sections.text: Seat counts in the admin console follow active users with a product seat, not every SCIM record. A deactivated user does not free a seat until the nightly reconcile. Administrators who need the seat the same day can release it from the user page.

sections.title: Lumen Desk identity provisioning, part 4
sections.text: Provisioning logs keep the external id, the Northstar id, and the result. They do not keep the identity provider's password or token. Tokens used by the SCIM client are rotated from the admin console and expire on a schedule the customer chooses.

sections.title: Audit export runbook, part 1
sections.text: Audit exports stream newline-delimited JSON to an object the customer can download for a limited time. Large tenants should slice by day. A single request that tries to hold a month of mailbox events in one response will hit the gateway even if the worker is healthy.

sections.title: Audit export runbook, part 2
sections.text: The export includes actor, action, object id, and time. It does not include message bodies. Customers who need bodies export them from the mailbox itself under their own retention rules.

sections.title: Audit export runbook, part 3
sections.text: A failed export can be resumed from the last completed hour. Resuming does not duplicate completed hours because the object names include the hour. Deleting an object and rerunning that hour is the way to repair a bad slice.

sections.title: Audit export runbook, part 4
sections.text: Compliance teams often compare the export count with the in-product counter. Those counts match when both use the same time zone. The export uses UTC. A local-midnight report will disagree at the edges of the day.

sections.title: Sandbox and demonstration tenants, part 1
sections.text: Sandbox tenants are disposable. The reset action deletes tickets, macros, and demo users in that tenant and does not touch production. The confirmation dialog requires the tenant name because the control used to sit too close to the demo-data loader.

sections.title: Sandbox and demonstration tenants, part 2
sections.text: Demonstration seeds recreate a scripted matter, a scripted inbox, and a set of sample customers inside the sandbox. They are fiction used for training. They are not account records and they are not contracts.

sections.title: Sandbox and demonstration tenants, part 3
sections.text: Sandbox data may be copied from a scrubbed production snapshot when a customer asks for a realistic test. The snapshot drops message bodies and replaces names. It is still not a source of refund authority.

sections.title: Sandbox and demonstration tenants, part 4
sections.text: Load tests belong in a sandbox with a separate ingest token. Production tokens that point at a sandbox will drop events. The error is recorded on the token, not on the customer's invoice.

sections.title: Tax documents and exemption files, part 1
sections.text: Harbor Billing stores exemption certificates per jurisdiction. A certificate must show the jurisdiction and a taxpayer id that matches the billing profile. A cropped scan that loses the stamp is treated as missing, and the invoice falls back to the default rate.

sections.title: Tax documents and exemption files, part 2
sections.text: Tax reversals are invoice corrections. They are not subscription refunds and they do not change the refund handbook. The correcting document references the original invoice id.

sections.title: Tax documents and exemption files, part 3
sections.text: Currency exponents live in a table Northstar maintains. A currency with no minor unit must be configured with exponent zero. A wrong exponent misstates amounts on the PDF even when the ledger integer is right.

sections.title: Tax documents and exemption files, part 4
sections.text: Credit memos calculate tax from the credited lines. They must not reuse the original invoice tax snapshot when only some lines are credited. Mid-cycle seat changes are the common case.

sections.title: Seat changes and proration, part 1
sections.text: Adding seats mid-cycle bills the new seats for the remaining time at the current plan price. Removing seats credits the unused time at the price the customer actually paid, not at the price of the plan they are moving to.

sections.title: Seat changes and proration, part 2
sections.text: A downgrade that changes both quantity and plan is two calculations. The unused portion uses the old price and the old quantity. The new portion uses the new price and the new quantity. Mixing those inputs under-credits the customer.

sections.title: Seat changes and proration, part 3
sections.text: The seat count on an invoice is the count at each change, not a single number for the month. A one-day overlap can appear when a change happens near the invoice boundary. The line dates show the overlap.

sections.title: Seat changes and proration, part 4
sections.text: Professional services milestones are not seats. They invoice when the milestone is completed. Reopening the task must not clear the invoiced flag. The flag is stored on the milestone id.

sections.title: Dunning and payment retries, part 1
sections.text: Dunning runs on a tenant schedule. Pausing a mailbox inside the customer's own email system does not pause Northstar. The tenant pause is a setting in Harbor Billing, and it has an end date so a freeze does not run forever.

sections.title: Dunning and payment retries, part 2
sections.text: Capture calls are not retried after a timeout. A timeout can mean the processor captured the payment and lost the response. Retrying can create a second authorization. Voids are used when a second authorization is still open.

sections.title: Dunning and payment retries, part 3
sections.text: Idempotency keys travel with the original attempt and with any retry that is actually safe. A retry without the key is treated as a new attempt. The payment log shows both keys when they differ.

sections.title: Dunning and payment retries, part 4
sections.text: Past-due notices name the invoice and the amount. They do not offer a refund and they do not change a signed window. A customer who wants a commercial exception still needs a signed document.

sections.title: Retention and legal holds, part 1
sections.text: Retention deletes data that has passed the age on the workspace. A legal hold stops deletion for the workspace named in the hold. A tenant-level interpretation was a defect. Holds do not spill into neighboring workspaces.

sections.title: Retention and legal holds, part 2
sections.text: The delete job writes a count of removed objects and a count of objects skipped because of a hold. Those counts are the way to see that a hold is scoped correctly. A skipped count of zero on a held workspace means the hold was not applied.

sections.title: Retention and legal holds, part 3
sections.text: Backups follow a shorter cycle than the customer's retention promise. A backup is not a way for a customer to recover data they asked to delete after the backup has aged out. Support does not restore deleted production data from a backup without a written request from an administrator.

sections.title: Retention and legal holds, part 4
sections.text: Exports taken before a deletion remain the customer's copy. Northstar does not reach into the customer's object storage to delete those copies. The retention policy describes Northstar's systems only.

sections.title: Quill report semantics, part 1
sections.text: Quill dimensions keep the fields the event mapping names. A URL dimension that keeps only the host will merge shops that share a host and differ by path. The shop id on the event is the safer dimension when the customer has more than one storefront.

sections.title: Quill report semantics, part 2
sections.text: Sampling is a project flag read when the ingest token is issued. A plan upgrade does not reissue the token. Customers who upgrade and still see sampling need a new token before the new rate applies.

sections.title: Quill report semantics, part 3
sections.text: Saved reports can expose columns that an old import left in the warehouse. The semantic layer is the control. Removing a column there removes it from previews. Row-level security still applies, including to test books if the test book is in the same dataset.

sections.title: Quill report semantics, part 4
sections.text: Report rebuilds for a past month read the archive, not the sampled store, when the archive still has the month. A rebuild changes the report. It does not change an invoice.

sections.title: Access reviews and offboarding, part 1
sections.text: Offboarding a user is incomplete while rules still name that user. The offboarding report lists inbox rules, escalation steps, and saved reports owned by inactive users. An administrator reassigns them. The report does not reassign them automatically, because the right destination is a local decision.

sections.title: Access reviews and offboarding, part 2
sections.text: Escalation policies should show a skipped step as skipped and should not treat the skip as the end of the policy when later steps are still live. A severity-one policy is expected to have two live steps. A weekly check looks for policies that do not.

sections.title: Access reviews and offboarding, part 3
sections.text: Session revocation is immediate for the user and does not delete tickets. An analyst who saw a sensitive column in a preview still has whatever they wrote down. The product control is to remove the column and revoke the session. It is not a promise that a person forgot the screen.

sections.title: Access reviews and offboarding, part 4
sections.text: Administrator invitations expire. An invitation that is forwarded to a personal mailbox can be accepted by the wrong person if the mailbox is shared. Customers are told to invite a named work account. Northstar does not police the customer's mail routing.
